brief: The entryway is the household's air lock - everything the outside world sends in passes through it twice a day. Its zones fail not from dirt but from unmade decisions: mail without a verdict, shoes without a cap, keys without a home. Run this room first; it is small, fast, and the daily payoff builds belief in the whole system.
tips: Organizer tipCap every category with a number, not a feeling: one coat per person on hooks, two pairs of shoes per person at the door, everything else upstairs or in the closet.

Cleaning tipThe entry mat does 80% of the room's cleaning. Vacuum it every reset, hose and dry it monthly, and replace it the moment it stops trapping grit - a worn mat exports dirt to every floor in the house.
Lean tipTreat mail as a single-piece flow: it goes from hand to verdict (act, file, recycle) in one touch. A mail pile is a queue, and queues in the entryway grow without limit.

zones.primary_function: Receive and launch daily essentials
zones.completed_state: A clear arrival surface with only current-day essentials in defined homes and no loose paper
zones.items_storage: keys, wallet, sunglasses, phone, mail, handbag, backpack, work badge. Typical storage approach: small tray, mail sorter, labeled hooks, charging dock.
zones.hazards: blocked exit path, trip hazards, overloaded outlets
zones.expert_cue: Place the tray where your hand naturally lands on entry - moving a key bowl 30 cm from the natural drop point is the difference between a system and a suggestion.

zones.primary_function: Store frequently used outerwear
zones.completed_state: Current-season outerwear is easy to retrieve and return, with off-season items relocated
zones.items_storage: coats, jackets, hats, scarves, gloves, umbrellas. Typical storage approach: hooks, hangers, upper shelf bins, umbrella stand.
zones.expert_cue: Hooks beat hangers for daily outerwear by a factor of ten in compliance; save hangers for the closet and occasion coats.

zones.primary_function: Contain footwear used near the entrance
zones.completed_state: Only current footwear remains, pairs are visible, and the walking path is clear
zones.items_storage: daily shoes, boots, slippers, shoe-care supplies. Typical storage approach: shoe rack, boot tray, labeled basket.
zones.hazards: trip hazards, wet footwear, blocked door
zones.expert_cue: Store soles-down on trays, current season only; a two-pairs-per-person cap at the door keeps the zone self-limiting.

zones.primary_function: Support short transition tasks
zones.completed_state: The surface supports one clear purpose and the interior storage is categorized
zones.items_storage: mail, decor, bags, pet items, small tools, seasonal accessories. Typical storage approach: shallow drawer dividers, baskets, tray.
zones.expert_cue: Keep the surface standard to three items or fewer - flat surfaces near doors are clutter magnets with a 24-hour relapse rate.

zones.primary_function: Provide a clean and safe threshold
zones.completed_state: The threshold is clean, unobstructed, functional, and ready for safe entry and exit
zones.items_storage: door hardware, doormat, floor mat, shoe debris, pet hair. Typical storage approach: defined mat boundary and no-storage floor rule.
zones.expert_cue: Two-mat systems (coarse outside, absorbent inside) capture the majority of tracked-in soil before it reaches the first rug.

brief: The kitchen is the highest-throughput workcell in the home, and it rewards 6S more than any other room. Every minute of prep, cooking, and cleanup crosses these seven zones, so small ergonomic wins compound daily. Sequence matters here: do the sink zone early - it is the recovery point every other zone drains into.
tips: Organizer tipArrange by workflow triangle: prep tools within one step of the prep counter, cooking utensils within arm's reach of the stove, and nothing in the triangle that isn't used weekly.
Cleaning tipDegrease before you sanitize - sanitizer can't reach through grease film. Warm water and dish soap first, then disinfectant with full label dwell time on food-contact surfaces.
Lean tipThe counter is production space, not storage. Every appliance that lives on it must earn its footprint with at least three uses a week; everything else goes to a cabinet garage or the pantry.

zones.primary_function: Prepare food on an open work surface
zones.completed_state: A mostly open counter with only active daily-prep tools and at least one full clear work area
zones.items_storage: cutting boards, knives, mixing bowls, small appliances, oils, utensils. Typical storage approach: counter boundary, knife storage, appliance homes.
zones.hazards: knife exposure, hot appliance clearance, cord hazards
zones.expert_cue: Clear counter is production capacity: a 60 cm clear run of workspace is the minimum viable prep zone - protect it like a fire lane.

zones.primary_function: Cook at the range, oven, or cooktop
zones.completed_state: Frequently used cooking tools are within safe reach and the cooktop area is clear
zones.items_storage: pots, pans, utensils, spices, oils, pot holders, timers. Typical storage approach: utensil crock, drawer dividers, spice rack, pan storage.
zones.expert_cue: Store by reach-while-cooking: oils, salt, and the three most-used utensils within one step of the burners; everything else is a drawer item.

zones.primary_function: Wash food, dishes, and hands
zones.completed_state: The sink is empty, clean, and ready; cleaning tools are sanitary and contained
zones.items_storage: dish soap, brushes, sponges, drying rack, dishwasher supplies. Typical storage approach: sink caddy, under-sink tray, drying boundary.
zones.expert_cue: An empty sink at day's end is the kitchen's keystone habit - it resets the whole room's standard while the coffee brews.

zones.primary_function: Store daily dishes and light serving items
zones.completed_state: Daily-use items are grouped, reachable, and retrievable without moving unrelated items
zones.items_storage: plates, bowls, cups, glasses, mugs, serving ware. Typical storage approach: shelf risers, category shelves, labels.
zones.expert_cue: Eye-level shelves are prime real estate: daily dishes there, occasional items above, and nothing you'd need a chair for more than monthly.

zones.primary_function: Store heavy cookware and larger kitchen tools
zones.completed_state: Cookware is nested or separated, lids are contained, and heavy items are stored low
zones.items_storage: pots, pans, lids, bakeware, colanders, mixing bowls. Typical storage approach: lid rack, pull-out shelves, pan dividers.
zones.expert_cue: Nest by size with lid organizers vertical; if a pot hasn't cooked in a year, it's donation inventory occupying your best low storage.

zones.primary_function: Store hand tools used for cooking and serving
zones.completed_state: Each drawer has one clear category and every tool fits within its divider
zones.items_storage: flatware, spatulas, peelers, measuring tools, foil, wraps, towels. Typical storage approach: drawer dividers, labels, quantity limits.
zones.expert_cue: Dividers first, then a hard rule: one of each tool unless you genuinely cook with two. Duplicate spatulas are how drawers die.

zones.primary_function: Preserve current food and make inventory visible
zones.completed_state: Food is current, grouped, dated where needed, and visible without overfilling
zones.items_storage: produce, dairy, meat, leftovers, condiments, frozen food, ice. Typical storage approach: clear bins, date labels, zones, first-in-first-out.
zones.expert_cue: Assign shelves by category and temperature - raw proteins low and sealed, leftovers at eye level with dates - and run a weekly eye-level purge before grocery day.

brief: A pantry is inventory management wearing a wooden costume. Its failure modes are the classic ones - overstock, expired stock, and stock nobody can see - and its fixes are classic too: first-in-first-out rotation, visible quantities, and a hard boundary between working shelf and backstock. A well-run pantry cuts grocery spend because you stop buying what you already own.
tips: Organizer tipDecant only where it pays: flour, sugar, rice, cereal. Everything else keeps its label - the package is free information about expiry dates and cooking instructions.
Cleaning tipCrumbs are livestock feed. Vacuum shelf corners and wipe with mild soap every reset, and inspect flour and grain containers for pantry moths while you shine.
Lean tipRun FIFO on every shelf: new stock loads behind, old stock pulls forward. Date-mark backstock with a marker on the lid - if you can't read the date from the doorway, it isn't marked.

zones.primary_function: Store grains, pasta, cereals, and shelf-stable staples
zones.completed_state: Staples are grouped, visible, dated as needed, and oldest items are used first
zones.items_storage: rice, pasta, cereal, grains, bread, tortillas. Typical storage approach: shelf labels, clear bins, turntables.
zones.expert_cue: Square, clear, airtight containers recover a third of shelf volume over factory packaging and make low-stock visible from across the room.

zones.primary_function: Store shelf-stable cans, jars, and sauces
zones.completed_state: Items are grouped by type, labels face forward, and damaged or expired containers are removed
zones.items_storage: canned vegetables, soups, sauces, beans, jars. Typical storage approach: tiered risers, shelf labels, FIFO rows.
zones.expert_cue: Front-face labels and rotate new stock to the back; a can riser turns three hidden rows into three visible ones.

zones.primary_function: Store baking ingredients and tools
zones.completed_state: Ingredients are sealed, labeled, grouped, and easy to inventory
zones.items_storage: flour, sugar, baking powder, chocolate, decorating supplies. Typical storage approach: airtight containers, bin labels, scoop storage.
zones.expert_cue: Kit the activity, not the ingredients: one bin that lifts out with flour, sugar, soda, and cutters turns setup into a single motion.

zones.primary_function: Support quick snacks and packed meals
zones.completed_state: Approved snacks are portioned or grouped and accessible to intended users
zones.items_storage: snack bars, chips, crackers, lunch bags, reusable containers. Typical storage approach: open bins, child-height zones, quantity limits.
zones.expert_cue: Make the healthy default the easy grab: kid-approved snacks in an open bin at kid height, portioned, with a visible refill trigger.

zones.primary_function: Hold reserve household food quantities
zones.completed_state: Backstock has a defined maximum and feeds forward into daily-use zones
zones.items_storage: duplicate staples, beverages, paper goods, bulk packages. Typical storage approach: dated bins, min-max labels, heavy items low.
zones.expert_cue: Backstock obeys two rules: dated on arrival, and pulled FIFO. Undated bulk is where savings go to expire.

brief: The dining room's central risk is mission drift: the table becomes a desk, the buffet becomes a filing cabinet, and dinner moves to the couch. This SOP restores the room to its actual function - shared meals - and gives the flat surfaces the quantity limits they need to stay clear between them.
tips: Organizer tipThe table's standing inventory is a centerpiece and nothing else. Homework, mail, and projects get a rolling caddy that arrives and leaves with the activity.
Cleaning tipDust the light fixture and chair rungs before the table - top-down order - and condition wood surfaces quarterly so spills bead instead of soaking.
Lean tipStore dishware by pull frequency, not by set: the plates you use daily belong at hand height in the kitchen; the china cabinet holds occasion-ware only, displayed and dust-controlled.

zones.primary_function: Provide a clear surface for meals and shared activities
zones.completed_state: The table is meal-ready with only intentional decor or current-use items
zones.items_storage: placemats, centerpiece, homework, mail, serving pieces. Typical storage approach: centerpiece boundary, no-drop rule, nearby action tray.
zones.expert_cue: The table's only permanent resident is the centerpiece; every activity that visits brings its own container and leaves with it.

zones.primary_function: Support serving and display
zones.completed_state: The surface has a defined serving area and limited decorative display
zones.items_storage: platters, candles, decor, beverage supplies, mail. Typical storage approach: display boundary, serving tray, drawer labels.
zones.expert_cue: Style in odd-numbered groups with breathing room - a surface that's 60% empty reads as intentional; 90% full reads as storage.

zones.primary_function: Store serving pieces and dining supplies
zones.completed_state: Items are grouped by use, protected, and accessible without restacking
zones.items_storage: table linens, serving bowls, platters, candles, utensils. Typical storage approach: shelf dividers, linen baskets, labels.
zones.expert_cue: Store table linens flat or rolled with the matching napkins inside the runner - one pull sets the table.

zones.primary_function: Protect and display special tableware
zones.completed_state: Displayed items are clean, intentional, secure, and not overcrowded
zones.items_storage: china, glassware, heirlooms, decorative serving pieces. Typical storage approach: shelf liners, display spacing, inventory label.
zones.expert_cue: Plate racks and cup hooks display safely; stacked china should never exceed eight plates or the bottom ones become load-bearing archaeology.

zones.primary_function: Prepare and serve beverages
zones.completed_state: The station is stocked to a defined level, clean, and ready for one-motion use
zones.items_storage: coffee maker, kettle, mugs, tea, barware, bottles. Typical storage approach: tray, mug hooks, labeled bins, cord management.
zones.expert_cue: Build the station in use-order - machine, pods/grounds, cups, stirrers, exit - and cap mugs at the number of drinkers plus two.

brief: The living room is shared territory with no single owner, which is exactly why it drifts. The remedy is visible standards everyone can read: a basket per category, a cable path per device, a clear circulation route wide enough for the vacuum. Aim for a room that resets in five minutes, because it will need to, nightly.
tips: Organizer tipOne basket per media category - remotes, throws, current magazines - and the basket's rim is the quantity limit. When it doesn't close or stack, something leaves.
Cleaning tipVacuum upholstery seams and under cushions monthly; that's where crumbs, coins, and allergens concentrate. Rotate and flip cushions on the same cadence to even the wear.
Lean tipRoute and label cables once, with velcro ties and a labeled power strip, and the media center stays auditable - you can spot a foreign cable or a missing remote at a glance.

zones.primary_function: Support comfortable conversation and relaxation
zones.completed_state: Seating is clear, textiles are limited and folded, and controls are easy to find
zones.items_storage: pillows, throws, remotes, reading materials, side baskets. Typical storage approach: remote tray, blanket basket, cushion standard.
zones.expert_cue: Lift cushions on every reset: the seams are the house's coin-and-crumb reservoir, and monthly rotation doubles cushion life.

zones.primary_function: Provide a small shared surface for active use
zones.completed_state: Most of the surface is open with one tray or defined display grouping
zones.items_storage: books, remotes, coasters, decor, toys, cups. Typical storage approach: tray boundary, coasters, daily reset cue.
zones.expert_cue: One tray defines the table's entire standing inventory; if it doesn't fit the tray, it doesn't live on the table.

zones.primary_function: Support television, audio, and entertainment devices
zones.completed_state: Devices are ventilated, cables managed, and accessories stored by system
zones.items_storage: television, speakers, remotes, game systems, cables, media. Typical storage approach: cable labels, remote home, ventilated bins.
zones.expert_cue: Label both ends of every cable at install; the 90 seconds per cable repays itself the first time anything gets moved or troubleshot.

zones.primary_function: Store books and intentional display items
zones.completed_state: Books and displays are grouped, dust-free, stable, and visually balanced
zones.items_storage: books, frames, plants, collections, decor. Typical storage approach: category sections, bookends, display limits.
zones.expert_cue: Shelve with 10-15% slack per shelf; a full shelf is a queue with no capacity, and the overflow lands on the nearest flat surface.

zones.primary_function: Provide personal convenience and task lighting
zones.completed_state: Each table supports a limited set of current-use items with managed cords
zones.items_storage: lamps, chargers, drinks, books, medicine, decor. Typical storage approach: small tray, cable clip, drawer divider.
zones.expert_cue: Wipe bulbs while dusting fixtures - a dusty bulb loses a noticeable share of its output, and lighting is the cheapest room upgrade there is.

zones.primary_function: Keep movement through the room safe and easy
zones.completed_state: Walkways are open, rugs lie flat, and floor items stay within defined boundaries
zones.items_storage: rugs, baskets, pet items, toys, cords, floor lamps. Typical storage approach: basket boundaries, rug grippers, no-storage paths.
zones.expert_cue: Walk the path with a laundry basket at reset: everything on the floor rides the basket to its real home. The path standard is full-width, always.

brief: The family room hosts the most competing activities per square meter in the house - media, play, games, crafts, charging - so its 6S depends on hard zone boundaries. Every activity gets a home base and a closing routine; the room works when a five-year-old can put it away, and only then.
tips: Organizer tipToy rotation beats toy storage: a third of the toys live here, two-thirds rest in labeled bins elsewhere. Fewer visible choices means deeper play and a three-minute pickup.
Cleaning tipDisinfect high-touch play surfaces and controllers weekly - they carry more biological load than the bathroom doorknob - and wash blanket-basket contents monthly.
Lean tipGive every game and puzzle a completeness check on reset day: missing-piece games are defects in inventory. Repair, cannibalize, or discard - never reshelve a broken set.

zones.primary_function: Support shared television, gaming, and streaming
zones.completed_state: Entertainment equipment is ready to use, ventilated, and reset after use
zones.items_storage: TV, consoles, controllers, remotes, headsets, media. Typical storage approach: controller dock, cable labels, media bins.
zones.expert_cue: Label both ends of every cable at install; the 90 seconds per cable repays itself the first time anything gets moved or troubleshot.

zones.primary_function: Support age-appropriate play and cleanup
zones.completed_state: Toys fit within defined categories and children can return them independently
zones.items_storage: toys, blocks, dolls, vehicles, play mats. Typical storage approach: picture labels, open bins, quantity limits.
zones.hazards: choking hazards, broken toys, trip hazards
zones.expert_cue: Open, labeled, picture-tagged bins at child height - and rotation, not volume, is what keeps play deep and pickup short.

zones.primary_function: Store shared games and puzzles
zones.completed_state: Complete games are visible, grouped, and stored so pieces remain contained
zones.items_storage: board games, cards, puzzles, dice, instruction sheets. Typical storage approach: shelf labels, zipper bags, vertical storage.
zones.expert_cue: Bag loose pieces inside each box and stack boxes horizontally; a completeness check on reset day keeps the shelf defect-free.

zones.primary_function: Store shared comfort textiles
zones.completed_state: Clean comfort items fit inside one defined container or shelf
zones.items_storage: blankets, throws, floor cushions, pillows. Typical storage approach: basket limit, folding standard.
zones.hazards: blocked vents, pet hair, overfilled baskets
zones.expert_cue: One basket, folded to a uniform size, capped at the rim - blankets multiply quietly and the basket is their honest census.

zones.primary_function: Charge family electronics in one controlled area
zones.completed_state: Devices and chargers are labeled, ventilated, and safely powered
zones.items_storage: tablets, phones, game controllers, chargers, headphones. Typical storage approach: charging dock, cord labels, timer or smart strip.
zones.hazards: battery heat, damaged cords, overloaded outlets
zones.expert_cue: One multi-port station in one location, cords labeled, with a house rule that devices sleep there - not in bedrooms.

zones.primary_function: Support casual projects and family activities
zones.completed_state: Supplies are grouped by activity and the work surface can be cleared quickly
zones.items_storage: paper, crayons, scissors, glue, kits, activity books. Typical storage approach: portable caddies, drawer bins, project tray.
zones.expert_cue: Kit supplies by project type in lidded, labeled bins, and enforce a one-project-out rule; craft chaos is always a WIP-limit problem.

brief: Sleep science and lean practice agree on the primary bedroom: fewer visible items, lower cognitive load, better rest. The zones here run from the two-minute nightstand to the ninety-minute closet, and the closet is the boss fight - schedule it when you're fresh, and let the seasonal-rotation standard do the heavy lifting afterward.
tips: Organizer tipThe nightstand standard is five items or fewer on top. Everything that supports sleep stays; everything that competes with it - especially the charging phone - finds a home across the room.
Cleaning tipWash pillows (not just cases) quarterly and vacuum the mattress surface and under-bed with the upholstery tool - dust mites concentrate where you breathe all night.
Lean tipRun the reversed-hanger experiment for one season: turn all hangers backward, flip them as items are worn, and let the unflipped hangers make your donation decisions for you.

zones.primary_function: Support restorative sleep
zones.completed_state: The bed is clean, made to a simple standard, and free of stored clutter
zones.items_storage: mattress, pillows, sheets, blankets, bedside textiles. Typical storage approach: linen set standard, under-bed limits.
zones.expert_cue: Make the bed to the standard every morning - it's the room's largest visual surface, and it sets the compliance tone for every other zone.

zones.primary_function: Support one sleeper's nighttime routine
zones.completed_state: Only current nighttime essentials remain and the surface is mostly clear
zones.items_storage: lamp, phone, charger, book, glasses, medication, water. Typical storage approach: small tray, cable clip, drawer divider.
zones.expert_cue: Five items or fewer on top; a small drawer tray keeps the inside from becoming the junk drawer's bedroom franchise.

zones.primary_function: Support one sleeper's nighttime routine
zones.completed_state: Only current nighttime essentials remain and the surface is mostly clear
zones.items_storage: lamp, phone, charger, book, glasses, medication, water. Typical storage approach: small tray, cable clip, drawer divider.
zones.expert_cue: Five items or fewer on top; a small drawer tray keeps the inside from becoming the junk drawer's bedroom franchise.

zones.primary_function: Support limited daily dressing or display
zones.completed_state: The top has one defined landing tray and no clothing backlog
zones.items_storage: jewelry, fragrance, decor, pocket contents, folded clothes. Typical storage approach: valet tray, jewelry organizer, display boundary.
zones.expert_cue: A single tray or valet for daily-carry items; the dresser top is the bedroom's landing zone and needs the same cap.

zones.primary_function: Store folded clothing by category
zones.completed_state: Clothing fits without compression, categories are visible, and drawers open freely
zones.items_storage: underwear, socks, sleepwear, shirts, workout clothes. Typical storage approach: drawer dividers, vertical folding, labels.
zones.expert_cue: File-fold vertically so every item is visible from above - stacked folding hides the bottom two-thirds of every drawer.

zones.primary_function: Store current wardrobe and accessories
zones.completed_state: Current clothing is visible, grouped, reachable, and contained within capacity
zones.items_storage: hanging clothes, shoes, bags, belts, seasonal items. Typical storage approach: matching hangers, shelf bins, shoe zones, labels.
zones.expert_cue: Group by type, then color; one hanger style throughout; and let the reversed-hanger test make the keep/donate calls data-driven.

brief: A guest room has two states - museum and hotel - and 6S keeps it permanently ready to flip. The standard is hotel logic: neutral surfaces, empty drawer space, and a small welcome kit, so that hosting requires fifteen minutes of freshening rather than an afternoon of excavation.
tips: Organizer tipReserve genuine guest capacity: one empty drawer, six empty hangers, and clear nightstand space. A guest room that stores your overflow is a storage room with a bed in it.
Cleaning tipEven unused rooms accumulate dust film and stale air. Between guests, run a monthly ten-minute shine - surfaces, sill, and a linen refresh - so the room never develops that unused smell.
Lean tipStage a standardized welcome kit (water glass, tissues, charger, wifi card, spare blanket) in one labeled bin. Setup becomes a checklist, not a scavenger hunt.

zones.primary_function: Provide clean and ready guest sleeping space
zones.completed_state: The bed is guest-ready and spare linens are complete and easy to find
zones.items_storage: sheets, pillows, blankets, mattress protector. Typical storage approach: guest linen set label, under-bed limit.
zones.expert_cue: Make the bed to the standard every morning - it's the room's largest visual surface, and it sets the compliance tone for every other zone.

zones.primary_function: Provide simple guest convenience
zones.completed_state: The surface is clear and offers only universal guest essentials
zones.items_storage: lamp, clock, charger, tissues, water coaster. Typical storage approach: guest tray, charger label.
zones.expert_cue: Five items or fewer on top; a small drawer tray keeps the inside from becoming the junk drawer's bedroom franchise.

zones.primary_function: Provide temporary clothing storage
zones.completed_state: At least one or two drawers are empty and remaining supplies are labeled
zones.items_storage: empty drawers, spare blankets, guest supplies. Typical storage approach: drawer labels, guest supply bin.
zones.expert_cue: Reserve at least one fully empty drawer for guests; the rest hold spare linens folded to a uniform footprint, not household overflow.

zones.primary_function: Provide hanging space and limited household storage
zones.completed_state: A defined section remains open for guests and household storage is contained
zones.items_storage: hangers, luggage rack, guest linens, overflow clothing. Typical storage approach: guest boundary, matching hangers, labeled bins.
zones.expert_cue: Group by type, then color; one hanger style throughout; and let the reversed-hanger test make the keep/donate calls data-driven.

zones.primary_function: Support unpacking, reading, or short work
zones.completed_state: The surface and floor area are open, functional, and free of household overflow
zones.items_storage: chair, small desk, luggage rack, welcome items. Typical storage approach: welcome tray, luggage boundary.
zones.expert_cue: Stage the guest kit - charger, wifi card, water glass, tissues - in one labeled bin so hosting is a checklist, not a hunt.

brief: A child's bedroom is a training ground for every 6S habit they'll ever have, which means the standards must be designed for their height, their reading level, and their attention span. Picture labels beat word labels, open bins beat lidded ones, and a closing routine beats every lecture ever delivered.
tips: Organizer tipSet homes at kid height: daily clothes in the bottom drawers, favorite toys on the lowest shelves. If a child needs an adult to put something away, the system - not the child - has failed.
Cleaning tipMake shine a two-song job: one song for surfaces with a microfiber cloth, one for floor pickup. Kids sustain what they can finish inside their attention span.
Lean tipPhotograph the standard state and tape the photo inside the door at eye level. 'Match the picture' is an audit a six-year-old can run without any adult arbitration.

zones.primary_function: Support sleep and bedtime routines
zones.completed_state: The bed is accessible, bedding is manageable, and sleep items are limited
zones.items_storage: bed, bedding, stuffed animals, nightlight. Typical storage approach: stuffed-animal limit, bedside basket.
zones.hazards: blocked egress, cords, excessive soft items
zones.expert_cue: Make the bed to the standard every morning - it's the room's largest visual surface, and it sets the compliance tone for every other zone.

zones.primary_function: Store bedroom toys and support independent cleanup
zones.completed_state: Toys fit in picture-labeled categories and the floor is clear
zones.items_storage: figures, dolls, blocks, vehicles, collections. Typical storage approach: open bins, picture labels, rotation bin.
zones.expert_cue: Open, labeled, picture-tagged bins at child height - and rotation, not volume, is what keeps play deep and pickup short.

zones.primary_function: Support homework, drawing, and school preparation
zones.completed_state: The work surface is clear, active work is contained, and supplies have homes
zones.items_storage: school supplies, laptop, books, papers, chargers. Typical storage approach: in-progress tray, supply cups, cable management.
zones.expert_cue: The surface standard is current-task tools plus one inbox tray; a reference photo taped nearby makes 'clear' unambiguous.

zones.primary_function: Store hanging clothes, shoes, and accessories
zones.completed_state: Current-size clothing is grouped and reachable at the child's height
zones.items_storage: shirts, dresses, jackets, shoes, backpacks. Typical storage approach: size labels, low hooks, shelf bins.
zones.expert_cue: Group by type, then color; one hanger style throughout; and let the reversed-hanger test make the keep/donate calls data-driven.

zones.primary_function: Store folded children's clothing
zones.completed_state: Current-size clothing fits, categories are simple, and drawers close easily
zones.items_storage: underwear, socks, pajamas, shirts, pants. Typical storage approach: picture labels, dividers, vertical folding.
zones.expert_cue: File-fold vertically so every item is visible from above - stacked folding hides the bottom two-thirds of every drawer.

zones.primary_function: Prepare items needed for school and activities
zones.completed_state: Tomorrow's essentials are together, current, and ready to leave
zones.items_storage: backpack, lunchbox, sports bag, instruments, permission slips. Typical storage approach: hooks, checklist, action folder.
zones.hazards: blocked floor, forgotten medication or forms
zones.expert_cue: Pack the launch zone the night before - bag on hook, shoes staged, forms signed - and the morning runs on rails.

brief: The nursery is the one room where 6S is genuinely about safety first and aesthetics a distant second. Every standard here serves a tired adult operating one-handed in the dark: supplies within reach of the changing pad, a bare-crib sleep standard, and chemical and cord hazards engineered out rather than managed.
tips: Organizer tipDesign the changing station for one-handed reach: diapers, wipes, and cream inside a 45-centimeter arc of the pad, restocked to a par level every evening.
Cleaning tipUse fragrance-free, infant-safe cleaners only, and launder crib linens on hot. Wipe the changing pad after every use; deep-clean it on the weekly reset.
Lean tipRun diaper backstock on a two-bin system: when the open bin empties, the reserve bin moves forward and the shopping list gets the trigger. You will never run out at 2 a.m. again.

zones.primary_function: Support safe infant sleep
zones.completed_state: The crib follows current safe-sleep guidance and contains no unnecessary items
zones.items_storage: crib, fitted sheet, sleep sack, monitor. Typical storage approach: sleep checklist, linen limit.
zones.expert_cue: The safe-sleep standard is a bare crib: fitted sheet only, nothing loose, mattress at the height the child's mobility requires.

zones.primary_function: Support diapering and immediate baby care
zones.completed_state: One-hand essentials are stocked within reach and hazards are secured
zones.items_storage: diapers, wipes, cream, changing pad, disposal supplies. Typical storage approach: drawer dividers, min-max labels, diaper caddy.
zones.expert_cue: Everything within one-handed reach of the pad, restocked to par each evening - one hand is always on the baby.

zones.primary_function: Store current-size infant clothing
zones.completed_state: Current-size clothing is visible, labeled, and outgrown items are routed out
zones.items_storage: onesies, sleepers, socks, seasonal layers. Typical storage approach: size labels, drawer dividers, next-size bin.
zones.expert_cue: Group by type, then color; one hanger style throughout; and let the reversed-hanger test make the keep/donate calls data-driven.

zones.primary_function: Support bottle or nursing preparation
zones.completed_state: Clean feeding supplies are separated, complete, and ready for the next use
zones.items_storage: bottles, pump parts, formula, bibs, burp cloths. Typical storage approach: clean/dirty separation, drying rack, labels.
zones.expert_cue: Separate clean-and-ready from used-and-waiting with two distinct bins; 2 a.m. is no time for ambiguity.

zones.primary_function: Hold reserve baby-care supplies
zones.completed_state: Backstock has clear minimum and maximum levels and feeds the changing station
zones.items_storage: diapers, wipes, toiletries, diaper pail liners. Typical storage approach: dated bins, size labels, min-max cards.
zones.expert_cue: Backstock obeys two rules: dated on arrival, and pulled FIFO. Undated bulk is where savings go to expire.

zones.primary_function: Support reading and low-stimulation play
zones.completed_state: A small curated set is reachable and easy to reset
zones.items_storage: board books, soft toys, sensory items. Typical storage approach: front-facing shelf, picture labels, rotation bin.
zones.expert_cue: Front-facing book display at floor level; a dozen visible covers out-perform fifty spines for a pre-reader.

brief: Bathrooms concentrate the home's moisture, chemistry, and expiry-date problems into its smallest rooms. The primary bath rewards ruthless sorting - cosmetics and medicines expire faster than anyone believes - and a shine discipline built on dwell time, ventilation, and drying the wet zones daily.
tips: Organizer tipCounter standard: daily-use items only, corralled on one tray you can lift with one hand to clean under. Everything used less than daily lives in a drawer or cabinet.
Cleaning tipSpray tub and shower cleaner first, then clean the rest of the room while it dwells - chemistry needs minutes, not muscle. Finish by squeegeeing glass and running the fan 20 minutes.

Lean tipCheck expiry dates on every Sort pass: most cosmetics carry a 6-24 month open-jar symbol, and expired sunscreen and medicine are defects, not inventory. Dispose of medicines via take-back, never the toilet.

zones.primary_function: Support daily hygiene and grooming
zones.completed_state: The counter is mostly clear with only daily-use items in defined positions
zones.items_storage: soap, toothbrushes, skincare, hair tools, cosmetics. Typical storage approach: daily tray, toothbrush holder, heat-tool rest.
zones.expert_cue: Daily items on one liftable tray, everything else in drawers - the counter should clean in one swipe.

zones.primary_function: Store personal-care tools and products
zones.completed_state: Products are current, grouped, divided, and visible without digging
zones.items_storage: makeup, razors, combs, brushes, dental supplies. Typical storage approach: drawer dividers, category labels, quantity limits.
zones.expert_cue: Drawer dividers by routine (morning, evening, weekly) and a hard expiry check every Sort pass - open cosmetics age in months, not years.

zones.primary_function: Store cleaning supplies and backstock around plumbing
zones.completed_state: Plumbing remains accessible and supplies are contained in pull-outs or turntables
zones.items_storage: cleaners, paper goods, toiletries, plumbing items. Typical storage approach: leak tray, slide-out organizers, turntable, labels.
zones.expert_cue: Two stacked pull-out bins double usable volume around the P-trap, and a leak-alert mat turns the cabinet floor into an early-warning system.

zones.primary_function: Store medicines and small daily-care items
zones.completed_state: Only current approved items remain, grouped by purpose and secured as needed
zones.items_storage: OTC medicine, first aid, eye care, prescriptions, grooming items. Typical storage approach: shelf labels, dated bins, lockable section.
zones.expert_cue: Medicines actually prefer a cool, dry bedroom shelf over a humid bathroom cabinet; either way, child-secure and expiry-checked twice a year, disposed via take-back.

zones.primary_function: Support bathing and routine cleaning
zones.completed_state: Only active products remain, surfaces are clean, and the floor is slip-resistant
zones.items_storage: shampoo, conditioner, soap, razors, toys, squeegee. Typical storage approach: caddy zones, bottle limit, hooks.
zones.expert_cue: Spray, then wait: cleaner dwell time does the scrubbing. Squeegee after each use and the weekly clean drops to minutes.

zones.primary_function: Support sanitation and replenishment
zones.completed_state: The area is clean, minimally stocked, and supplies are contained
zones.items_storage: toilet paper, brush, cleaner, trash can, hygiene supplies. Typical storage approach: reserve-roll limit, brush home, lined bin.
zones.expert_cue: Brush and bowl treatment weekly with full dwell; keep a dedicated cloth color for toilet-only duty and never let it near a counter.

zones.primary_function: Store towels, washcloths, and bathroom linens
zones.completed_state: Linens are clean, complete, folded by type, and held within capacity
zones.items_storage: bath towels, hand towels, washcloths, mats. Typical storage approach: shelf labels, folding standard, set quantities.
zones.expert_cue: Three sets per person or bed - one in use, one in wash, one on shelf - folded to a uniform footprint, sets nested in a pillowcase.

brief: The guest bath is the room visitors judge and the household forgets. Its 6S is mercifully small - five zones, hotel-grade standards - and its sustain trigger is simple: a five-minute reset before anyone visits and a weekly shine whether anyone does or not.
tips: Organizer tipStock it like a hotel: backup toilet paper visible without hunting, fresh hand towel, soap above half-full, and a small bin - and nothing personal on the counter.
Cleaning tipEven low-traffic toilets grow biofilm rings. Weekly bowl treatment with full dwell time, plus a monthly pour of water down seldom-used drains to keep the trap sealed against sewer gas.
Lean tipLaminate a five-line reset checklist inside the vanity door. Guest-ready becomes a two-minute verified state, not a scramble triggered by the doorbell.

zones.primary_function: Support simple guest hygiene
zones.completed_state: The counter is clean, welcoming, and limited to universal guest essentials
zones.items_storage: soap, tissues, hand towel, toothbrush cup, small decor. Typical storage approach: guest tray, hand-towel hook, refill cue.
zones.expert_cue: Daily items on one liftable tray, everything else in drawers - the counter should clean in one swipe.

zones.primary_function: Store guest toiletries and cleaning backstock
zones.completed_state: Guest supplies are easy to find and cleaning products are safely separated
zones.items_storage: toilet paper, spare soap, toiletries, cleaners. Typical storage approach: labeled guest bin, cleaning bin, leak tray.
zones.expert_cue: Drawer dividers by routine (morning, evening, weekly) and a hard expiry check every Sort pass - open cosmetics age in months, not years.

zones.primary_function: Provide clean bathing space for guests
zones.completed_state: The bathing area is clean, dry, stocked lightly, and free of abandoned products
zones.items_storage: shampoo, soap, curtain, towels, bath mat. Typical storage approach: guest caddy, hook labels, bottle limit.
zones.expert_cue: Spray, then wait: cleaner dwell time does the scrubbing. Squeegee after each use and the weekly clean drops to minutes.

zones.primary_function: Provide clean sanitation and reserve supplies
zones.completed_state: The toilet area is clean and has one visible reserve roll plus contained backstock
zones.items_storage: toilet paper, brush, cleaner, trash can. Typical storage approach: reserve-roll standard, brush home.
zones.expert_cue: Brush and bowl treatment weekly with full dwell; keep a dedicated cloth color for toilet-only duty and never let it near a counter.

zones.primary_function: Provide clean towels and backup linens
zones.completed_state: A complete guest set is visible and excess linens are removed
zones.items_storage: bath towels, hand towels, washcloths, bath mat. Typical storage approach: guest-set basket, folding standard.
zones.expert_cue: Three sets per person or bed - one in use, one in wash, one on shelf - folded to a uniform footprint, sets nested in a pillowcase.

brief: The laundry room is a genuine production line - sort, wash, dry, fold, return - and it jams exactly where factories jam: at the fold step, where work-in-progress piles up. This SOP fixes the flow with staged sorting, a clear folding surface with a same-day rule, and machines that get maintained like the equipment they are.
tips: Organizer tipSort at the source with a three-bag hamper station (lights, darks, delicates) so a load starts machine-ready. The floor in front of the washer is a landing zone, not a queue.
Cleaning tipMachines need shine too: empty the lint trap every load, scrub the detergent drawer and door gasket monthly, and run a hot cleaning cycle to stop mildew odor at its source.
Lean tipInstitute the same-day fold rule - a dryer buzzer is an andon signal, not a suggestion. Folded-and-returned inside 24 hours is the standard that keeps WIP at zero.

zones.primary_function: Wash and dry household textiles
zones.completed_state: Machines are clean, accessible, empty, and ready for the next load
zones.items_storage: washer, dryer, lint screen, hoses, machine cleaners. Typical storage approach: load-status card, lint reminder, machine-clear rule.
zones.expert_cue: Lint trap every load, gasket and detergent drawer monthly, hot maintenance wash monthly - machine care is fire prevention wearing chore clothing.

zones.primary_function: Store laundry chemicals and stain tools
zones.completed_state: Current products are contained, labeled, and stored safely within quantity limits
zones.items_storage: detergent, bleach, softener, stain remover, measuring tools. Typical storage approach: chemical bin, dosing labels, child-safe placement.
zones.expert_cue: Store concentrates on a drip tray at adult height, measured with the cap's actual line - overdosing detergent causes most 'my machine smells' complaints.

zones.primary_function: Separate dirty laundry by household method
zones.completed_state: Dirty laundry fits within defined categories and the floor remains clear
zones.items_storage: hampers, baskets, delicates bags, pocket contents. Typical storage approach: labeled hampers, pocket tray, fill limits.
zones.expert_cue: Three-way sort at the source (lights, darks, delicates) means any full bag is a machine-ready load with zero re-handling.

zones.primary_function: Fold, pair, and prepare clean laundry for return
zones.completed_state: The surface is clear between loads and no clean-laundry backlog remains
zones.items_storage: clean laundry, folding board, baskets, hangers. Typical storage approach: return baskets, folding boundary, timer cue.
zones.expert_cue: The folding surface carries a same-day rule: what lands folds, what folds returns. It is a workstation, not a shelf.

zones.primary_function: Dry items that should not enter the dryer
zones.completed_state: Air-dry items fit without crowding and are removed promptly when dry
zones.items_storage: drying rack, hangers, delicates, drip-dry items. Typical storage approach: hanger limit, drip tray, dry-date tag.
zones.expert_cue: Cap the rod: when hanging space is full, the oldest items move on - a full rod is a queue pretending to be storage.

zones.primary_function: Store tools used to maintain the laundry area
zones.completed_state: Cleaning tools are secure, dry, and easy to retrieve without blocking machines
zones.items_storage: broom, mop, vacuum attachments, rags, trash bags. Typical storage approach: wall hooks, labeled caddy, floor boundary.
zones.expert_cue: Hang tools handle-up on a rail - bristles and heads that touch the floor deform and re-soil; nothing stores wet.

brief: The home office is where physical clutter and digital debt shake hands. Its 6S extends the method to paper flow - act, file, or shred, with one inbox tray as the only legal landing spot - and to the desk itself, which is a workstation with a standard, not a horizontal shelf with a keyboard.
tips: Organizer tipDesk-surface standard: the tools of the current task plus one inbox tray. When the task changes, the desk resets - the standard is a photograph, not a mood.
Cleaning tipElectronics shine safely: powered down, microfiber cloth, screen-safe cleaner sprayed on the cloth never the screen, and compressed air for the keyboard monthly.
Lean tipGive paper a one-touch triage - act, file, shred - and empty the inbox tray on a Friday cadence. A filing backlog is hidden work; the tray's rim is its WIP limit.

zones.primary_function: Support focused computer and knowledge work
zones.completed_state: The desk has a clear work area, current work is contained, and cords are controlled
zones.items_storage: computer, monitor, keyboard, notebook, phone, current papers. Typical storage approach: inbox, action tray, cable clips, device dock.
zones.expert_cue: The surface standard is current-task tools plus one inbox tray; a reference photo taped nearby makes 'clear' unambiguous.

zones.primary_function: Store frequently used office tools
zones.completed_state: Each drawer has one purpose, usable supplies are visible, and duplicates are limited
zones.items_storage: pens, notebooks, stapler, chargers, sticky notes, personal items. Typical storage approach: drawer dividers, labels, quantity limits.
zones.expert_cue: Top drawer: daily tools in a tray. Deep drawer: hanging files. Anything unfiled after Friday's inbox-empty is a process escape.

zones.primary_function: Retain and retrieve required documents
zones.completed_state: Files are current, labeled, protected, and easy to retrieve by a simple system
zones.items_storage: tax records, warranties, household records, project files. Typical storage approach: retention labels, folder taxonomy, shred bin.
zones.expert_cue: File by retrieval question ('where would I look?'), purge on a yearly cadence, and scan anything you'd only ever need as information rather than paper.

zones.primary_function: Store reference books and intentional display
zones.completed_state: Reference material is grouped and accessible, with stable and uncluttered shelves
zones.items_storage: books, binders, manuals, awards, decor. Typical storage approach: category labels, bookends, archive limits.
zones.expert_cue: Shelve with 10-15% slack per shelf; a full shelf is a queue with no capacity, and the overflow lands on the nearest flat surface.

zones.primary_function: Print, scan, and process paper
zones.completed_state: Equipment is ready, supplies are stocked to a defined level, and paper flow is clear
zones.items_storage: printer, scanner, paper, ink, envelopes, cables. Typical storage approach: paper bins, ink label, scan tray, cable labels.
zones.expert_cue: Stage paper and cartridges at point of use with a min/max on the shelf edge; a printer pantry three rooms away is motion waste.

zones.primary_function: Store office consumables and backup tools
zones.completed_state: Supplies are categorized, counted, and limited to realistic use
zones.items_storage: paper, pens, tape, folders, labels, envelopes, tech accessories. Typical storage approach: clear bins, min-max cards, shelf labels.
zones.expert_cue: One open of each consumable, backstock behind, min/max labels on the shelf - office supplies obey pantry rules.

brief: The garage is the home's warehouse, and it fails like one: no aisles, no addresses, no rotation. The transformation lever is vertical - walls and overhead take the storage, the floor keeps only wheeled and parked things - plus honest sorting of the museum of abandoned projects. Budget more time here than anywhere else, and take before photos; the payoff deserves evidence.
tips: Organizer tipZone the walls by activity - auto, garden, sport, tools - and give every hook and shelf an address. The parking footprint is sacred: if the car can't enter, the garage has failed its primary function.
Cleaning tipDegrease the floor once properly (degreaser, stiff brush, absorbent on stains), then sweep monthly. A clean floor makes new leaks - car, water heater, chemicals - instantly visible.
Lean tipOverhead racks hold only labeled, dated, seasonal bins under 15 kg. If a bin comes down less than once a year two years running, its contents are donation candidates by rule.

zones.primary_function: Support repairs, assembly, and household projects
zones.completed_state: The work surface is mostly clear and only one active project occupies the zone
zones.items_storage: hand tools, project parts, adhesives, fasteners, bench tools. Typical storage approach: project tray, tool shadowing, bench boundary.
zones.expert_cue: End every session with a cleared bench - the bench is capacity, and tomorrow's project deserves a clean start with visible tool status.

zones.primary_function: Store frequently used hand tools
zones.completed_state: Tools are visible, secure, grouped by use, and returned to defined homes
zones.items_storage: hammers, screwdrivers, pliers, wrenches, saws, measuring tools. Typical storage approach: pegboard outlines, drawer labels, lockable cabinet.
zones.hazards: falling tools, sharp edges, child access
zones.expert_cue: Shadow boards turn 'is anything missing?' into a two-second glance; outline the silhouettes and the tools will police themselves.

zones.primary_function: Store powered tools, chargers, and batteries
zones.completed_state: Tools are clean, batteries are safely charged, and accessories stay with their tool family
zones.items_storage: drills, saws, sanders, chargers, batteries, accessories. Typical storage approach: tool cases, battery rack, charger labels, ventilation.
zones.hazards: battery heat, damaged cords, blade access
zones.expert_cue: Store batteries at partial charge in a cool spot, off the chargers; label each tool's home and keep guards on at rest.

zones.primary_function: Store supplies used for vehicle maintenance and cleaning
zones.completed_state: Automotive supplies are contained, labeled, leak-free, and separated from household products
zones.items_storage: fluids, jumper cables, tire tools, cleaners, rags, funnels. Typical storage approach: spill tray, chemical cabinet, shelf labels.
zones.expert_cue: Fluids upright on a drip tray, rags in a sealed metal can, and a spill kit (absorbent, gloves, bag) staged before you need it.

zones.primary_function: Store seasonal and active recreation equipment
zones.completed_state: Equipment is grouped by activity and current-season gear is easiest to access
zones.items_storage: balls, helmets, bikes, skis, camping accessories, coolers. Typical storage approach: ball bins, wall racks, seasonal labels.
zones.hazards: falling gear, blocked exits, helmet damage
zones.expert_cue: Store by season with a hard changeover date; ball racks and vertical hooks recover floor space that bins never will.

zones.primary_function: Store yard tools and outdoor maintenance supplies
zones.completed_state: Long tools are secured, chemicals are separated, and the floor path is open
zones.items_storage: rakes, shovels, trimmers, hoses, fertilizers, pots. Typical storage approach: wall tracks, hose reel, locked chemical shelf.
zones.expert_cue: Long tools hang head-up on a rail; sharpen and oil at end of season and spring setup starts with tools that work.

zones.primary_function: Store infrequently used household reserve items
zones.completed_state: Every container is labeled, weight is appropriate, and access does not require unsafe climbing
zones.items_storage: seasonal decor, coolers, folding chairs, archive bins, bulk paper goods. Typical storage approach: large labels, location map, weight limits, dated review.
zones.hazards: falling bins, ladder use, overloaded racks
zones.expert_cue: Overhead holds only labeled, dated, seasonal bins under 15 kg - and never anything you'd need in a hurry or in the dark.

brief: The workshop is where 6S was born - Toyota's factories, scaled to a bench. Shadow boards, point-of-use tooling, and hard chemical segregation aren't aesthetics here; they're the difference between a hobby that builds things and one that loses fingers. The Safety pass in this room is the most important fifteen minutes in the manual.
tips: Organizer tipShadow-board the hand tools: outline every silhouette so a missing tool announces itself before cleanup ends. Point-of-use beats category - the square lives at the saw, not in a drawer of squares.
Cleaning tipSawdust is a slip hazard, a fire load, and a finish-ruiner. Vacuum rather than sweep (sweeping airborne-launches the fines), and empty dust collection at every session's end.
Lean tipStore finishes and solvents in a fire-rated cabinet, rags in a sealed metal can - oily rags self-ignite - and stage PPE at the door so wearing it costs zero extra steps.

zones.primary_function: Support fabrication, repair, and detailed project work
zones.completed_state: The bench is ready for one project, with tools returned and scrap removed
zones.items_storage: bench tools, measuring tools, vise, project parts, lighting. Typical storage approach: tool boundary, project tray, task lighting standard.
zones.hazards: sharp tools, moving equipment, eye hazards
zones.expert_cue: End every session with a cleared bench - the bench is capacity, and tomorrow's project deserves a clean start with visible tool status.

zones.primary_function: Store portable and stationary power tools
zones.completed_state: Tools are clean, secured, complete, and stored with accessories
zones.items_storage: saws, drills, routers, sanders, grinders, cords. Typical storage approach: tool cases, wall mounts, lockout tags, labels.
zones.hazards: blade access, damaged guards, electrical hazards
zones.expert_cue: Store batteries at partial charge in a cool spot, off the chargers; label each tool's home and keep guards on at rest.

zones.primary_function: Store small parts used in projects
zones.completed_state: Small parts are labeled by type and size and can be inventoried at a glance
zones.items_storage: screws, nails, bolts, nuts, washers, anchors, hinges. Typical storage approach: drawer cabinets, bin labels, sample fasteners.
zones.expert_cue: Small-parts organizers labeled by size and type, one compartment per SKU; a mixed-fastener coffee can is a ten-minute search tax on every project.

zones.primary_function: Store usable project materials
zones.completed_state: Materials are stable, sorted by type and length, and scrap limits are enforced
zones.items_storage: lumber, metal, sheet goods, pipe, trim, offcuts. Typical storage approach: rack labels, cut-length bins, scrap boundary.
zones.expert_cue: Store lumber flat and supported every 40 cm, offcuts vertical in a bin with a size floor - below the floor, it's kindling, not inventory.

zones.primary_function: Store paints, solvents, adhesives, and finishes
zones.completed_state: Products are current, sealed, labeled, ventilated, and safely separated
zones.items_storage: paint, stain, glue, solvent, brushes, rags. Typical storage approach: flammable cabinet, date labels, spill tray.
zones.expert_cue: Fire-rated cabinet, original containers, incompatibles separated, and oily rags in a self-closing metal can - spontaneous combustion is real and patient.

zones.primary_function: Provide immediate access to protective equipment
zones.completed_state: Required PPE is visible, clean, current, and reachable before work begins
zones.items_storage: safety glasses, hearing protection, gloves, masks, first aid, fire extinguisher. Typical storage approach: silhouette board, inspection dates, signage.
zones.expert_cue: PPE lives at the door, sized to each user, inspected on the reset - wearing it must cost zero extra steps or it won't happen.

brief: The mudroom is the entryway's industrial-strength sibling: same launch-and-land function, triple the throughput, plus pets, sports gear, and weather. Its standards must survive a wet Tuesday at 7:40 a.m. - which means hooks over hangers, open bins over lidded ones, and a floor that forgives.
tips: Organizer tipOne labeled hook-and-bin column per family member turns 'whose is this?' into a solved problem, and makes the owner of any drift instantly visible.
Cleaning tipTrap grit at the threshold: bristle mat outside, absorbent mat inside, boot tray for wet footwear. Vacuum the trays and shake the mats every reset - grit is sandpaper for your floors.
Lean tipStage tomorrow tonight: bags packed on hooks, shoes in the launch position, signed forms in the bag. The morning rush is a process problem, and it is solvable.

zones.primary_function: Store daily coats, bags, and outerwear
zones.completed_state: Each person has a limited, labeled hook area and the floor stays clear
zones.items_storage: coats, backpacks, handbags, hats, scarves. Typical storage approach: name labels, hook limits, seasonal rotation.
zones.expert_cue: One labeled column per person, hooks at their height - ownership visible from the doorway ends the daily whose-is-this arbitration.

zones.primary_function: Support sitting, changing shoes, and short-term staging
zones.completed_state: The seat is usable and temporary items leave by the next routine cycle
zones.items_storage: bench, bags, mail, sports gear, pet items. Typical storage approach: seat-clear rule, action basket, timer cue.
zones.expert_cue: Keep the surface standard to three items or fewer - flat surfaces near doors are clutter magnets with a 24-hour relapse rate.

zones.primary_function: Contain active outdoor footwear
zones.completed_state: Current footwear fits the rack or tray and wet items dry safely
zones.items_storage: boots, shoes, slippers, cleats, shoe-care items. Typical storage approach: boot tray, family labels, quantity limit.
zones.expert_cue: Store soles-down on trays, current season only; a two-pairs-per-person cap at the door keeps the zone self-limiting.

zones.primary_function: Support daily pet departures and care
zones.completed_state: Daily pet items are together, sanitary, and ready to grab
zones.items_storage: leashes, waste bags, collars, towels, food travel gear. Typical storage approach: hooks, labeled caddy, towel basket.
zones.expert_cue: Food sealed in an airtight bin with a scoop, leash-and-bag kit on its own hook, and a towel staged for wet-paw weather.

zones.primary_function: Store weather-specific family accessories
zones.completed_state: Only current-season gear is accessible and off-season items are relocated
zones.items_storage: gloves, hats, umbrellas, sunscreen, insect repellent. Typical storage approach: seasonal bins, picture labels, rotation date.
zones.expert_cue: Run a dated changeover checklist with photos; off-season gear stores clean, dry, labeled, and out of prime reach zones.

zones.primary_function: Store tools for maintaining the entry and adjacent spaces
zones.completed_state: Tools are secure and supplies are contained without blocking traffic
zones.items_storage: broom, mop, vacuum, cleaners, rags. Typical storage approach: wall clips, caddy, chemical separation.
zones.expert_cue: Hang tools handle-up on a rail - bristles and heads that touch the floor deform and re-soil; nothing stores wet.

brief: The hall closet is the household's dark warehouse - highest density, lowest visibility, no owner. Its 6S rests on sightlines and stock control: clear bins, labels facing out, par levels for consumables, and a strict eviction rule for anything that merely 'ended up' there.
tips: Organizer tipFold linens to one uniform footprint and store sets nested inside their own pillowcase - one grab equals one complete bed change, and the shelf stays legible.
Cleaning tipClosed dark spaces breed mustiness: empty and wipe shelves on the reset, and leave the door cracked after cleaning sprees so trapped humidity escapes.
Lean tipSet par levels for paper goods and bulbs - min and max quantities written on the shelf edge. Below min triggers the shopping list; above max means stop buying it.

zones.primary_function: Store household sheets, towels, and blankets
zones.completed_state: Linens are complete, folded by type, and contained within shelf capacity
zones.items_storage: sheet sets, towels, blankets, pillowcases. Typical storage approach: shelf labels, set bundles, quantity standards.
zones.expert_cue: Three sets per person or bed - one in use, one in wash, one on shelf - folded to a uniform footprint, sets nested in a pillowcase.

zones.primary_function: Store vacuum and larger cleaning tools
zones.completed_state: Equipment is ready, attachments stay together, and access is unobstructed
zones.items_storage: vacuum, attachments, mop, broom, bucket. Typical storage approach: wall clips, attachment bag, floor boundary.
zones.expert_cue: Hang tools handle-up on a rail - bristles and heads that touch the floor deform and re-soil; nothing stores wet.

zones.primary_function: Store approved household cleaning products
zones.completed_state: Products are current, grouped, labeled, and secured as needed
zones.items_storage: sprays, disinfectants, cloths, gloves, trash bags. Typical storage approach: portable caddy, shelf liner, labels.
zones.expert_cue: Group by room-of-use in carry caddies, never mix chlorine and ammonia products on the same shelf, and keep everything in original labeled containers.

zones.primary_function: Store reserve paper goods and household consumables
zones.completed_state: Backstock follows defined minimum and maximum levels and remains visible
zones.items_storage: toilet paper, tissues, paper towels, light bulbs, batteries. Typical storage approach: min-max cards, clear bins, shelf labels.
zones.expert_cue: Backstock obeys two rules: dated on arrival, and pulled FIFO. Undated bulk is where savings go to expire.

zones.primary_function: Store infrequent guest or seasonal items
zones.completed_state: Items are labeled, dated, and kept within a fixed capacity
zones.items_storage: extra pillows, seasonal decor, guest blankets, travel items. Typical storage approach: dated bins, shelf map, category labels.
zones.expert_cue: Run a dated changeover checklist with photos; off-season gear stores clean, dry, labeled, and out of prime reach zones.

brief: The stair landing is a circulation space that clutter loves precisely because no one owns it. Its 6S is short and strict: the path stays clear at full width, the 'going upstairs anyway' pile gets a single contained basket, and the safety pass - lighting, handrail, tread edges - protects the most injury-prone route in the house.
tips: Organizer tipIf items must stage here, allow exactly one stair basket per direction with a same-day empty rule. The steps themselves are never storage - not for one book, not for one morning.
Cleaning tipVacuum tread edges and corners where grit collects, and wipe the handrail - it's a high-touch surface that almost never sees a cloth.
Lean tipAudit the landing at light-switch height: bulbs at full brightness, switch reachable at both ends, nothing casting a shadow on the top or bottom step.

zones.primary_function: Provide limited support without becoming a drop zone
zones.completed_state: The surface has one defined purpose and no deferred clutter
zones.items_storage: small decor, mail, keys, books, baskets. Typical storage approach: small tray, no-drop sign, daily reset cue.
zones.expert_cue: Keep the surface standard to three items or fewer - flat surfaces near doors are clutter magnets with a 24-hour relapse rate.

zones.primary_function: Display art or family items safely
zones.completed_state: Displays are secure, intentional, clean, and do not crowd the passage
zones.items_storage: frames, art, mirrors, sconces, hooks. Typical storage approach: spacing standard, secure anchors.
zones.expert_cue: Check frame hardware while you dust - stairway walls take vibration, and a level, secure gallery is both shine and safety.

zones.primary_function: Provide safe movement between levels
zones.completed_state: Every step and landing is completely clear, well lit, and slip-resistant
zones.items_storage: stairs, runner, lighting, gates, temporary items. Typical storage approach: no-storage rule, lighting check, gate standard.
zones.expert_cue: Walk the path with a laundry basket at reset: everything on the floor rides the basket to its real home. The path standard is full-width, always.

brief: Outdoor zones live under a maintenance clock that indoor rooms don't: UV, moisture, and temperature swings turn deferred care into replacement costs. This room's 6S leans hard on Shine-as-inspection - checking rail integrity, board condition, and grill grease while cleaning - and on a seasonal Standardize that matches storage to the calendar.
tips: Organizer tipStore cushions and textiles in a ventilated deck box the moment they're dry - UV and dew age fabric faster than use ever will. Covers go on furniture that stays out.
Cleaning tipDegrease the grill's grease tray and drip pan every few cooks, not every few months - accumulated grease is the number-one cause of grill fires.
Lean tipRun the seasonal changeover as a checklist with dated photos: what's out, what's covered, what's stored. Spring setup becomes an hour of restoration instead of a weekend of archaeology.

zones.primary_function: Support outdoor relaxation and conversation
zones.completed_state: Furniture is clean, stable, arranged for movement, and cushions are protected
zones.items_storage: chairs, cushions, tables, throws, covers. Typical storage approach: furniture layout marks, cushion bin, cover labels.
zones.expert_cue: Lift cushions on every reset: the seams are the house's coin-and-crumb reservoir, and monthly rotation doubles cushion life.

zones.primary_function: Support safe outdoor cooking
zones.completed_state: Cooking tools are ready, grease is removed, and combustibles are kept clear
zones.items_storage: grill, fuel, tools, thermometer, trays, cleaning brush. Typical storage approach: tool hooks, fuel boundary, cleaning checklist.
zones.expert_cue: Store by reach-while-cooking: oils, salt, and the three most-used utensils within one step of the burners; everything else is a drawer item.

zones.primary_function: Support meals and serving outdoors
zones.completed_state: The table is clean and meal-ready with clear circulation around it
zones.items_storage: table, chairs, placemats, serving tray, lighting. Typical storage approach: serving tray, chair positions, lighting cue.
zones.expert_cue: Choose a weather-rated standing setup and cover it; anything that can't live outside earns a home in the deck box, not a permanent spot on the table.

zones.primary_function: Maintain containers and nearby plants
zones.completed_state: Plants are healthy, supplies are contained, and drainage is clear
zones.items_storage: pots, soil, watering can, fertilizer, hand tools. Typical storage approach: tool caddy, plant labels, watering schedule.
zones.expert_cue: Long tools hang head-up on a rail; sharpen and oil at end of season and spring setup starts with tools that work.

zones.primary_function: Store cushions, toys, tools, and seasonal patio items
zones.completed_state: Stored items are dry, labeled, pest-free, and fit within the container
zones.items_storage: deck box, cushions, games, covers, small tools. Typical storage approach: deck-box categories, moisture check, labels.
zones.expert_cue: Ventilated, off the ground, and chemical-segregated - deck boxes and sheds follow garage rules with extra moisture vigilance.

zones.primary_function: Maintain structural and walking surfaces
zones.completed_state: Surfaces are clean, stable, clear, and free from slip or structural hazards
zones.items_storage: deck boards, railings, steps, lights, rug, drainage. Typical storage approach: inspection tags, no-storage paths, light check.
zones.expert_cue: Push-test the rail at every shine: movement, soft wood, or popped fasteners are a stop-and-fix, not a note-for-later.
